newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open mostly unchanged on Friday, although some traders said prices may soften in line with modest losses in London overnight.

London cocoa futures eased early Friday, but trading was exceedingly light as Ivory Coast and many European markets were closed for the Assumption Day holiday. At the midday break, LIFFE September was down five stg, to 1,009 stg, after trading in a tight 1,010-1,006 stg range. December was four stg weaker, at 1,039 stg.

On Thursday, New York cocoa ended lower in quiet trade, with active December falling $11 a tonne, to $1,516, after ranging from $1,532 to $1,511. Spot September ended $14 lower, at $1,485, while the back months lost $9 to $10.
September/December ended at $31 compared with $28 at the close on Wednesday.
On the charts, traders said December would face support near $1,510 and $1,500. Resistance was seen at $1,528-$1,532, with the next level at $1,543-$1,545.
